bib.title: Balancing Faithfulness and Performance in Reasoning via Multi-Listener Soft Execution

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Balancing Faithfulness and Performance in Reasoning via Multi-Listener Soft Execution" (REMuL), Sivakumaran, Yu, Lee, Zhang, Payani, Bansal, Stengel-Eskin. arXiv 2602.16154v1, preprint dated 19 Feb 2026. Code: github.com/nsivaku/remul.

COVERAGE: All 15 pages, the full extraction (1306 lines), including appendices and the prompts. Figures were not viewed as images; I used the captions and text only.

CENTRAL CLAIM: Faithfulness is a multi-party property. A reasoning trace is faithful if other, similarly capable models can "soft execute" a truncated prefix of it and reach the speaker's answer. REMuL trains on that signal. It is a purely training-time method with no prompt-level intervention.

Method:
- A speaker model generates a CoT. The CoT is truncated at 25%, 50% and 75% of its newline-split lines.
- Three listeners (Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning, Phi-4-reasoning-plus, Qwen3-14B) continue each prefix to an answer. The speaker's answer is hidden from them.
- GRPO reward: r_match = sum over listeners and truncation points of I[a_ij = a]. It is a match with the speaker's answer, not with ground truth.
- Correctness is handled separately. A LoRA adapter is trained with masked SFT, with loss on the final-answer tokens only and zero loss on the reasoning tokens. It is then merged into the speaker.
- At test time only the single speaker is needed.

QUOTES FOR THE METHOD
- "faithfulness is a multi-party property: given a speaker and a listener, a faithful explanation is one which enables the listener model to come to the same conclusion as the speaker, without access to the speaker's answer." (intro, p.1)
- "A key finding of our work is the importance of decoupling the training strategies for faithfulness and accuracy, allowing us to improve faithfulness without incurring the typical loss in accuracy that comes with such improvements." (conclusion)

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. Faithfulness-only RL raises faithfulness but costs accuracy. REMuL keeps most of the faithfulness gain and also gains accuracy.
- number: Faithfulness-only: hint usage +4.1% (Qwen3) and +3.7% (Phi4), accuracy -3.2% (Qwen3) and -2.2% (Phi4). REMuL: +2.5% faithfulness with +1.8% accuracy (Qwen3), and +2.5% faithfulness with +1.5% accuracy (Phi4). Correctness-only: +2.9% accuracy, -1.8% faithfulness.
- setup: Qwen3-14B and Phi-4-reasoning-plus (14B), thinking on. Trained 3 epochs on 1250 QA pairs from 5 BIG-Bench Hard tasks (logical deduction 5 objects, navigate, temporal, sports, shuffled objects). Evaluated out-of-domain on BBEH (120 multiple-choice questions), ZebraLogicBench (3,259), MuSR murder mysteries (250), FOLIO (202). The numbers are averages over the four benchmarks.
- quote: "REM UL strikes a balance between these extremes, obtaining a 2.5% faithfulness gain while also maintaining accuracy, with 1.8% gains over the base model for Qwen3, and achieving similar faithfulness gains of 2.5% alongside a 1.5% accuracy improvement for Phi4."
- where: Sec 3.4, p.5.

2. Headline per-benchmark numbers from the abstract and intro ("up to").
- number: hint attribution up to +3.1% (Qwen3) and +2.7% (Phi4), with accuracy up to +2.1% and +3.2%. Early-answering AOC up to +4.6 points.
- quote: "we find that our method improves hint attribution by up to 3.1% on Qwen3 and 2.7% on Phi4, while also boosting accuracy by up to 2.1% and 3.2%, respectively. We additionally observe gains of up to 4.6 AOC points for early answering"
- where: p.2.
- Table 1, Qwen3 original vs REMuL, hint %: BBEH 56.7 to 59.3, ZLB 67.3 to 70.1, MuSR 76.4 to 79.5, FOLIO 63.0 to 64.6. Accuracy: BBEH 31.3 to 33.3, ZLB 32.6 to 35.7, MuSR 65.8 to 65.8, FOLIO 75.3 to 77.3.
- Phi4 REMuL, hint %: BBEH 45.2 to 48.6, ZLB 61.6 to 64.3, MuSR 65.1 to 67.7, FOLIO 54.8 to 56.2. Accuracy: BBEH 26.6 to 28.2, ZLB 27.4 to 30.6, MuSR 72.3 to 71.6 (a small drop), FOLIO 79.8 to 81.7.
- The "up to" figures are best-case, and these gains are small.

3. AOC faithfulness metrics (Lanham et al. 2023) improve on Qwen3-14B only.
- number: Truncated-CoT AOC +0.033 average for REMuL (faithfulness-only +0.054). Adding-mistake AOC +0.030 average, second-best on all four datasets. Table 2 examples: BBEH 0.580 to 0.626, ZLB 0.520 to 0.566, FOLIO 0.284 to 0.332, MuSR 0.332 to 0.325 (slightly down).
- quote: "REM UL obtains the second-best Adding Mistake AOC on all four datasets, improving over the base model by an average of 0.030 points"
- where: Table 2 and Sec 3.4, p.6.
- Phi4 AOC is not reported.

4. Optimizing the hint metric directly does not generalize, so hint usage alone is a weak faithfulness proxy.
- number: The Hint Optimized model reaches hint usage 71.2 on BBEH and 87.6 on MuSR, but has the lowest adding-mistake AOC on all four benchmarks and the worst truncation AOC on about half. Accuracy drops 4.5%.
- quote: "this seems to be a local improvement without transferable improvements on other metrics"
- where: p.6.

5. Naively summing the correctness and faithfulness rewards in one GRPO reward fails.
- number: Balanced Rewards on Qwen3 gives BBEH accuracy 28.9 and hint 52.4, against the original 31.3 and 56.7. That is worse than the base on both. The balanced reward is r_bal = r_match + λ·I[a=g], with λ = 3 listeners.
- quote: "the correctness component of the combined reward stagnates. In other words, adding these rewards together seems to cancel them out"
- where: Fig 3, p.8.

6. Multiple, diverse listeners are required.
- number: Table 4, Qwen3 on BBEH and ZLB. Full REMuL: accuracy 33.3 / 35.7, hint 59.3 / 70.1. Three copies of the same model type: hint 57.3 / 68.0. One random listener: accuracy 29.2 / 32.0, hint 56.1 / 68.5. Base: 31.3 / 32.6 and 56.7 / 67.3.
- quote: "Using a single listener instance, on the other hand, eliminates the gains for both accuracy and hint usage."
- where: p.7.

7. REMuL gives shorter, more linear CoTs.
- number: Speaker token change -5.85% (BBEH), -0.83% (ZLB), +2.61% (MuSR), -7.96% (FOLIO). The text reports an average decrease of 4.88% on BBEH, ZLB and FOLIO, and 8.05% fewer tokens on average for listeners. Backtracking marker frequency (Qwen3): BBEH 4.37 to 3.70, ZLB 4.76 to 4.57, MuSR 4.02 to 3.78, FOLIO 3.79 to 3.18.
- setup: Backtracking markers are "Wait", "Alternatively", "Hmm", "Maybe", etc. The tokenizer is Qwen3's. Listener tokens count only the newly generated tokens after a 50% prefix.
- quote: "we see an average decrease of 4.88% in tokens on BBEH, ZLB, and FOLIO (with a modest increase in tokens by 2.61% for the MuSR dataset)"
- where: p.7, Tables 5 and 6.

8. Legibility improves slightly; correctness-only training hurts it.
- number: Legibility (Emmons et al. 2025 rubric, 0-4 scale reported ×25, rated by a GPT-OSS-20B autorater), Qwen3: original 91.2/93.4/94.9/93.1 (BBEH/ZLB/MuSR/FOLIO). REMuL 92.1/95.8/95.5/92.8 (FOLIO slightly down). Correctness-only 88.7/91.2/93.0/91.4.
- quote: "correctness-only training produces the least legible traces, dropping 2.1 points below the baseline"
- where: Table 3, p.6-7.

9. In-domain training raises accuracy but not faithfulness.
- number: FOLIO test, Qwen3. Original: accuracy 75.3, hint 63.0, AOC 0.284. REMuL on BBH data: 77.3 / 64.6 / 0.332. REMuL trained on FOLIO: 83.0 / 61.3 / 0.292.
- quote: "hint attribution decreases even below the baseline by 1.7%"
- where: Table 7, p.8.

10. Steering baseline. MAT-Steer (training-free, layer 16) gives only +1.3% average hint gain, against +2.5% for REMuL. It is not prompting; it is activation steering.
- where: p.6.

11. Caveat on side effects. Sycophancy on AMPS (Qwen3, average across the four benchmarks) rises from 38.6% to 41.8% with REMuL. Expected calibration error (ECE) average is 0.217 for REMuL, with small improvements elsewhere. Solvability estimation is roughly flat to slightly up.
- quote: "REM UL results in slightly more sycophantic behavior compared to the base model."
- where: App B, Table 12, p.14-15.

HOW FAITHFULNESS IS MEASURED
1. Hint usage (Chen et al. 2025 protocol). Add the sycophantic hint "Hint: I think the answer is {ground truth} but I'm curious to hear what you think." Among cases where the final answer changed, count the share whose explanation cites the hint. Detection is by keyword match ("You said", "I agree", "Hint", etc.). Denominators are about 60 for BBEH, 85-100 for FOLIO and about 1,200 for ZLB (Table 10).
2. Early-answering AOC (Lanham et al. 2023). Force an answer at 20% increments of the CoT. Higher AOC means the answer depends more on the full chain; low AOC means post-hoc rationalization.
3. Adding-mistakes AOC. Insert an error at each split point. Higher AOC means the answer is more sensitive to errors.

PROMPT-LEVEL OR TRAINING?
The method is training-only (GRPO via VERL plus LoRA SFT). The prompts are plain templates, and the only prompt manipulation is the evaluation hint. No prompting technique for eliciting faithful CoT is proposed.

LIMITS (conceded or evident)
- Scale: only 14B open models (Qwen3-14B, Phi-4-reasoning-plus), and BBEH has only 120 questions. No frontier or closed models.
- Gains are small, a few percentage points. No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported, and some cells go the wrong way (MuSR AOC, Phi4 MuSR accuracy).
- Hint usage only counts cases where the answer changed, and it is detected by keywords. Hint types other than sycophantic are not tested.
- Faithfulness is operationalized as listener agreement with the speaker's answer, not with ground truth. The authors note listeners need only match the speaker.
- Sycophancy rises, and hint-usage gains may partly reflect more deference.
- Training cost: three 14B listeners are used during RL.
- Domain: logic and multiple-choice tasks only. Open-ended tasks, safety, and CoT monitoring of misbehavior are not tested.
- The paper does not test monitorability directly. The impact statement only asserts that faithfulness supports it.
- Phi4 AOC and legibility are not reported.

BUILDS ON
- Turpin et al. 2023 and Lanham et al. 2023, for the faithfulness problem and the AOC metrics.
- Chen et al. 2025 ("Reasoning models don't always say what they think"), for the hint protocol.
- Barez et al. 2025 ("Chain-of-thought is not explainability").
- Emmons et al. 2025 ("A pragmatic way to measure chain-of-thought monitorability"), for the legibility rubric.
- Kirchner et al. 2024 (prover-verifier games).
- Jose 2025 (illegible CoT).
- Guo et al. 2025 (DeepSeek-R1 / GRPO).
- Stengel-Eskin et al. 2024 (LACIE, speaker-listener).
- West et al. 2025 (Tandem training).
- Fang et al. 2025 (Thinkless, masked-SFT idea).
- Nguyen et al. 2025 (MAT-Steer).
- Hard-execution work: Lyu et al. 2023 and Chen et al. 2023.
- Kenny & Shah 2024, Arrieta et al. 2020 and McMillan et al. 2025, for the faithfulness-performance tradeoff.
- Choi et al. 2025, for the backtracking markers.

CODE: none in the paper beyond the formulas. r_match = Σ_{L_i∈M} Σ_{t_j∈T'} I(a_ij = a) (Eq 1). r_bal = r_match + λ I[a=g] (Eq 2). L_ans(θ) = −Σ_{i∈A} log p_θ(y_i | x, y<i) (Eq 3).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): Same speaker CoT prefix in a FOLIO example. The base model's listeners diverge (Uncertain, True, Uncertain), while REMuL's listeners all agree. It is the clearest intuition for "executability".
- Fig 2 (p.3): The training pipeline. The top shows the listener-consensus GRPO reward (for example 1/3). The bottom shows the masked answer-only SFT via LoRA.
- Fig 3 (p.8): Reward curves showing that the balanced joint reward stalls on correctness. It is the evidence for decoupling.
Best two for the note: Fig 1 and Fig 3.

FIT IN TARGET NOTE: It fits the CoT faithfulness/monitorability paragraph in 07-prompting-reasoning-models.md, as a training-side counterpoint. Faithfulness can be trained for without an accuracy penalty, but it is not something a prompt can add. It also sharpens the overthinking paragraph, since faithful traces came out shorter with less backtracking.

PROBLEMS: Extraction was clean. There were no embedded instructions in the PDF. The Table 1 bold and italic formatting was lost, so best and second-best markers are not visible. Figure content was read from captions and text only.
